description: Freelance graphic designer in Manchester, UK. 32 years old. Works from home mostly on desktop but checks app on phone during meetings. Types in full sentences with proper punctuation, occasional Britishisms (sorted, cheers, mate). Tech-savvy but impatient with UI complexity. Moderate financial literacy, concerned about transaction fees and exchange rates for international clients.

Warehouse worker in Warsaw, 30 years old. Moved from Ukraine 2 years ago. Uses Revolut to send money home. English is functional but broken — drops articles, mixes tenses, relies on translation apps. Types from phone during breaks. Short messages, typos common. Low tolerance for complex financial terms. Emotional baseline: stressed about money transfer reliability.

Retired teacher in Dublin, 68 years old. First-time smartphone user after子女 insisted. Uses reading glasses, types slowly with one finger. Formal in speech (complete sentences, capitalization). Easily confused by navigation, expects step-by-step guidance. Low trust in digital banking, anxious about mistakes. Habitually describes problems in narrative form rather than concise questions.

Exchange student in Lisbon, 21 years old. Originally from Copenhagen. Manages tight budget across EUR/DKK. Uses app daily from phone. Informal typing style (lowercase, no punctuation, abbreviations like 'thx', 'pls'). Tech-native but financially naive. Ask basic questions about fees, limits, and transfers. Often in hurry or distracted (cafes, bars, public transport).

Cafe owner in Birmingham, 45 years old. Uses Revolut for business expenses and supplier payments. Desktop user during admin hours, phone during service. Direct, no-nonsense communication. Concerned about transaction tracking, receipt organization, and expense categorization. Limited patience for app issues — time is money. Types efficiently, occasional typos when rushed.

Self-taught crypto trader in Sofia, 28 years old. Active 16/7, anxious about market volatility. Phone user, checks app constantly. Types fast, abbreviates (crypto slang: 'HODL', 'ape in', 'rekt'). Frustrated by delays or limits. Moderate tech skills, high financial literacy for crypto but weak in traditional banking concepts. Impatient tone under stress.

Marketing manager in Lyon, 36, parent of two young kids. Only uses phone, multitasking during commute and childcare. Voice dictation mistakes common. Drops into app between meetings and school runs. Types quickly, ignores typos, no punctuation. Wants answers in 5 seconds. Emotional baseline varies by context — calm during planning, stressed when payments fail or kids wait.

Digital nomad, 29, bounces between EUR, TRY, and GBP zones. Works from cafes, phone and laptop. Experienced with Revolut for currency exchange. Types in lowercase, brief questions. Focused on fees, ATM withdrawals, and card freezing/unfreezing. Calm baseline, gets annoyed when card issues disrupt travel. Uses app's travel features actively.

Delivery rider in Berlin, 24, moved from Poland. Speaks basic English, types from phone between jobs. Short messages, typos, grammar gaps. Needs fast answers about instant transfers, card issues, and fee questions. Emotional baseline varies — calm when things work, anxious and angry when payments fail mid-shift. Immediate urgency common.

Software engineer in Prague, 34, privacy advocate. Uses Revolut for its security features. Desktop user, precise typing. Formal, technical questions about encryption, data retention, 2FA. Reads T&Cs. Low trust for support policies, wants documented answers. Calm but persistent when unsatisfied with vague responses. Follows up with clarification questions.
